name: Isabel Doyle
life: “I still remember saving for a reception bigger than the flat I lived in.” Monday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Isabel knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I have been saving for a huge wedding. Hearing these two haggle over chairs has made me question mine.
appearance: Isabel has an aquiline nose and a square chin. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a rust-colored canvas coat with a small enamel bird on the lapel. In conversation Isabel takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: Isabel listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To change the plan for a future wedding.
family: Harold Byrd is Isabel’s cousin raised in the same household. Isabel chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Harold brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A ship without postcards*, Harold says, “I mailed a receipt for lunch. My family has been asking what an ordinary day costs.”
connections: Ida Heath. A guest choosing firm ground gives another future bride a useful approach to planning.

reactions.situation: A guest brings additional people to the boardwalk wedding
reactions.response: Isabel checks whether the couple can actually feed and seat the additional people.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Isabel writes down the shift time accurately, then helps them explain the circumstances without having to tell the whole room.
